To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The primary cosmic-ray energy is underestimated by about 20% for energies below 10^18.5 eV and overestimated by about 20 % for energies above 10^18 eV.

the calorimetric method is the most accurate and robust way to determine the energy of cosmic rays detected by the atmospheric fluorescence technique, that the method has an accuracy of about ±10% at the 10 ^{19} eV level, and that the method has a bias that can be determined to within 1%.
the calorimetric energies of air showers are systematically lower than the primary energies, and that the difference is about 15% for the highest energies.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the energy of a cosmic-ray event is given by the energy measured by the calorimetry method, plus a correction factor that depends upon the zenith angle and the primary mass, and a correction for the energy lost by the primary particle in its passage through the atmosphere.
the method is sound and reliable, and that the corrections are well understood.

the energy of the primary particle is the energy that is deposited in the atmosphere, but that this energy must be corrected for several effects, including the fact that only a portion of the shower particles reach the ground and that the atmosphere is not a perfect calorimeter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the energy assigned to a cosmic ray is the calorimetric shower energy multiplied by an energy scaling factor, which is a function of zenith angle and energy.
the corrections to the calorimetry are small, and the energy resolution of the method is excellent.
the energy resolution of the air fluorescence technique is about 20% at energies around 10 ^{19} eV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the corrections are not large, even at the highest observed cosmic-ray energies.
the energy of the primary cosmic ray is underestimated if only the calorimetric method is used.
